text:
maria: Quick heads-up — CI long-chat load shows steady memory growth on node groups that serve multi-hour contexts. Looks like KV cache fragmentation + small-block churn.

akshay: Saw that too. Got a flamegraph?

maria: Pasted a tiny profile snapshot from the latest run: 
```
peak_rss: 48.2GB
heap_used: 39.8GB
kv_cache_total: 22.4GB
kv_cache_free_frag: ~28%
avg_block_size: 1.2KB
most_allocs: tiny 256/512 bytes
```
Notable: tail of long contexts creates lots of short-lived allocations inside the slab allocator, but free lists are fragmented so reuse fails.

ben: Hmm. That avg_block_size of 1.2KB screams that our block sizing is mismatched for the key distribution. Are we splitting pages eagerly?

maria: Current allocator: fixed chunk classes [256,512,1k,2k,4k], plus a small buddy coalescer that only runs on full-page reclaim. We suspect long contexts interleave many unique kv inserts so holes appear between sizes.

eli: Would adaptive splitting help? e.g. if a large slot gets a lot of small entries, split it into smaller lanes to improve packing. But splitting has overhead.

akshay: Proposed two low-risk experiments: 
1) "adaptive-splitter-v1": eager split large blocks when >75% of payloads in that block are <512B (background cheap scan).
2) "evict-window": increase recency-weighted eviction window to prefer reclaiming blocks with high fragmentation score.

maria: I ran a quick A/B on synthetic long-context workload (50k unique keys per context, churn=0.8). Results (30m run):
```
baseline: peak_kv: 22.4GB, free_frag: 28%, qps: 120
splitter-v1: peak_kv: 18.7GB, free_frag: 14%, qps: 118
evict-window: peak_kv: 20.1GB, free_frag: 17%, qps: 119
splitter+evict: peak_kv: 17.9GB, free_frag: 12%, qps: 117
```
So splitter gives most reduction; small perf hit (~2-3% qps).

ben: Nice. What about CPU/latency? background splitting could add jitter.

maria: CPU increased ~6% peak on the affected nodes; p50 latency stable, p99 had a handful of +8–12ms spikes during split bursts.

eli: We should consider making splitting opportunistic and rate-limited. Also add a fast path: if a request hits a split block and we can satisfy from sub-block w/o locking, avoid full split.

akshay: Agree. I sketched a patch: do background histogram per slab segment, only split when histogram indicates >70% small entries and current free_frag >20%. Also throttle to 1 split/segment/sec. Patch is in my branch: `kv/adaptive-split-2026` (WIP).

maria: Another issue: compaction currently happens during full GC which we only trigger when free < 5%. That explains why fragmentation accumulates long-term. Maybe add an incremental compactor that merges adjacent free blocks lazily during low load.

ben: I'm wary of copy-heavy compaction in the hot path. Maybe a two-tier compactor: cheap coalesce of same-size adjacent free blocks (pointer fixup only), and a background copy-compact for mixed-size gaps.

eli: Also look at block-size tuning: add a 768B class between 512 and 1k? The distribution has a bump around 700B per traces. Adding midpoints can reduce slack.

maria: Good call. Quick experiment: adding 768B class reduced free_frag by ~3% on the synthetic test but increased allocator metadata by ~0.7% memory overhead. Net win for these workloads.

akshay: Action items:
- akshay: iterate splitter patch with throttling + fast-path (ETA 2d)
- ben: prototype cheap coalescer that only touches free lists (no copy) and measure GC pauses (ETA 3d)
- eli: run long 48h soak with splitter+coalescer once both patches are merged in staging (need infra-bot to carve a nodepool)
- maria: collect traces and create a perf+regression dashboard for this change set (p99/p999, memory, CPU)

ben: infra-bot can you create a dedicated staging pool for the soak?

infra-bot: created nodepool `kv-frag-soak-2026` (6 x A100), credentials posted to #eng-infra-deploys.

maria: Also thought: when sequence length grows > X (e.g., 30k tokens) we could switch to a different KV packing policy (aggressive compact-on-evict) since those contexts tend to be long-lived. Might be an orthogonal knob.

eli: That would be neat — context-aware packing policy. Let's prototype after splitter/coalescer.

akshay: I'll open PRs with tests + perf harness. Posting links once ready.

maria: Thanks all. If we can get splitter+coalescer in staging this week and a 48h soak next week, we should have good data to decide on adding 768B class and background compactor.

ben: Sounds good. I'll document expected regressions and rollback plan in the PR. :thumbsup:

maria: closing loop — good momentum here.
